Article 19 is about preserving evidence created during operation. Providers retain automatically generated high-risk AI logs to the extent those logs are under their control.

## Key Requirements

**Retain logs**: Keep relevant automatically generated records.

**Traceability**: Understand what happened and under what conditions.

**Six-month baseline**: The general minimum period is six months unless other law provides otherwise.

**Data protection**: Retention must still respect privacy and data-protection requirements.

**Financial institutions**: Existing regulated documentation arrangements may be relevant.

**Shared environments**: Clarify control, access and retention when logs sit with deployers or SaaS providers.

## Why Article 19 Matters

Article 19 helps translate the EU AI Act into clearer expectations for accountability, evidence, oversight and responsible operation. The requirement matters because AI governance is credible only when responsibilities and controls are understood and applied in practice.

## Real-World Example

An insurance AI records relevant inputs, outputs and actions. If those logs are under the provider’s control, the provider retains them under an appropriate governed schedule.

## Key Takeaway

**Documentation tells how a system was built. Logs tell how it behaved.**
